Plot a Hasselmann stochastic climate simulation

Source: R/hasselmann.R
plot.hasselmann_sim.Rd

Visualizes the Hasselmann climate model using time series, phase space, power spectrum, or ice-temperature relationship representations.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'hasselmann_sim'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("timeseries", "phase", "spectrum", "ice_temp"),
  var = c("T", "Td", "I"),
  n_points = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Object of class "hasselmann_sim" from hasselmann_sim.

type

Type of plot:

"timeseries"

Time series of selected variable (default)

"phase"

3D plotly visualization of T-Td-I space

"spectrum"

Power spectral density showing red noise character

"ice_temp"

Temperature-ice scatter with equilibrium curve

var

Variable to plot for timeseries/spectrum: "T" (surface temperature, default), "Td" (deep ocean), or "I" (ice extent).

n_points

Maximum number of points to plot; if NULL, plots all points. Useful for large simulations.

...

Additional arguments passed to internal plot functions.

Value

Returns the plot object invisibly (ggplot2 or plotly depending on type).

Details

The Hasselmann model produces red noise spectra characteristic of climate variability, with the deep ocean acting as a low-pass filter. Different plot types reveal different aspects of the stochastic climate dynamics.

The spectrum plot shows power spectral density on log-log axes, with a theoretical red noise reference (dashed line). The ice-temperature plot shows the relationship between surface temperature and ice extent, with the equilibrium curve I_eq(T) = max(0, -μT) shown as a dashed line.

The 3D phase plot (requires plotly) shows the trajectory in the full T-Td-I state space, revealing the attractor structure.

See also

hasselmann_sim for simulation, hasselmann_batch for forcing scenarios.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Simulate stochastic climate variability
sim <- hasselmann_sim(F_forcing = 0, n_steps = 200000, seed = 42)

# Inspect results
print(sim)
summary(sim)

# Different visualization types
plot(sim)                    # Time series of temperature
plot(sim, type = "phase")    # 3D phase space (plotly)
plot(sim, type = "spectrum") # Power spectrum
plot(sim, type = "ice_temp") # Ice-temperature relationship
} # }
